summary: The team is juggling a major SEO push for Asia Star and Intelligent China, a Knowledge website redesign, and urgent event logistics for the Women's Leadership Forum, while resolving a lingering email lockout.
summaryDetail: The top priority is the global marketing strategy: we're targeting top-five AI/search rankings for China programs within seven months, with Asia Star and Intelligent China as the flagship programs and US partnerships on hold. Joseph needs to deliver the target areas and audience profiles, and the team must provide the conversion tracking brief so SEO can start tracking. The Knowledge website redesign is moving forward with a clear direction—keep the two-menu structure, integrate BCI/BSI indices, and display more articles—but Joseph, Julie, and the team lead need to hold a 30-minute feedback session and Joker must implement changes. This week, urgent event tasks include finalizing the Nov 13 registration list (Shengjia Di crosschecking job titles by noon), Xuan drafting Professor Tao's briefing email, and Johnny creating the Chinese webpage for the Women's Leadership Forum; meanwhile, the team must also resolve the Outlook lockout by updating passwords on all devices and confirming the backend unlock. Looking ahead, the anniversary infographic discussion (Ira, Joseph, Julie) and Joseph's summary of Flow Design improvements are on the horizon, and the cancelled EuroCham event frees up capacity to focus on these initiatives.

decisions.text: Stale saved passwords on devices caused the account lockout; all devices must be updated.
Remove the standalone videos section; videos will be dispersed by topic across the site.
Keep the two-menu structure (Knowledge menu and School menu).
Bring BCI and BSI indices banners into the Knowledge section, similar to the school homepage.
Do not add a stock-market ticker at the top of the page.
Display more articles on the homepage using a pinned article plus latest/more-articles sections.
Prioritize Asia Star and Intelligent China as top two programs; Berkeley as optional third priority.
Put US partnership programs (Stanford, Columbia) on hold initially, focusing on China programs first.
Target top-five ranking for China programs in AI/search results within seven months.
Cancel the CKGSB–EuroCham Shanghai event scheduled for November 13.
